land.text: 'modern Yunnan ... the region around the Dian Lake' (the page names no boundary)

successors.note: Annexed by Han under Emperor Wu in 109 BCE; the Han seal made its king 'King of Dian' (Shizhaishan seal). Han's Yizhou commandery is the infobox successor.

capitals.name: Dian Lake basin (seat not named; royal cemetery at Shizhaishan, Jinning)
capitals.note: The Dian page names no capital and its infobox capital is empty; the point is the Dian Lake shore near the Shizhaishan cemetery where the seal was found (excavated 1954), a stand-in for the seat.

correction.text: 'modern Yunnan ... the region around the Dian Lake' (the page names no boundary)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Dian). The page puts the kingdom 'in modern Yunnan, southwestern China, in the region around the Dian Lake'; infobox area empty, so no comparison. Radius 120 km round Kunming is the researcher's stand-in for the lake basin; Qiongdu lay to the north, Yelang to the east, the Laojin and Mimo were allies.

region.text: 'modern Yunnan ... the region around the Dian Lake' (the page names no boundary)

ledger.note: 279 BC: Zhuang Qiao founds the Dian kingdom at Dian Lake. 'It was established in 279 BCE when King Qingxiang of Chu sent a military force to the southwest'; the Chu general 'decided to stay in Yunnan and adopt the native ways, establishing the Dian kingdom'. (The infobox and 'Dian culture' lines go back to the 8th century BCE; the state is dated by Sima Qian.)

region.text: 'modern Yunnan ... the region around the Dian Lake' (the page names no boundary)

ledger.note: 109 BC: Han annexes Dian. 'The Dian kingdom was annexed by the Han under the reign of Emperor Wu of Han in 109 BCE'; Han troops from Ba and Shu 'wiped out the Laojin and Mimo, leading the king of Dian to surrender'.

region.text: 'modern Yunnan ... the region around the Dian Lake' (the page names no boundary)

ledger.note: 109 BC: the Dian kingdom ends; the king receives the Han gold seal ('King Dian's Seal', found at Shizhaishan) and the land becomes Han's Yizhou commandery.

wars.name: Han conquest of Dian

zones.text: 'modern Yunnan ... the region around the Dian Lake' (the page names no boundary)

wars.outcome: Han victory: Han troops from Ba and Shu destroyed the allied Laojin and Mimo and the king of Dian surrendered in 109 BCE; Dian became Yizhou commandery.
wars.note: Lead-up: Emperor Wu sent envoys in 122 BCE; the Yelang neighbour submitted in the Nanyue campaign of 111 BCE (Yelang page).

certainty.note: No boundary is documented; the lake basin and its allies only. Soft throughout.

sources.title: Dian Kingdom
sources.note: Identity, the 279 BCE establishment by a Chu force, Yelang and Qiongdu neighbours, the 122 BCE Han envoys, the 109 BCE Han annexation and the King of Dian seal; no capital, no area.

sources.title: Yelang
sources.note: Neighbour Yelang west Guizhou: Chu's Zhuang Qiao expedition 'early third century BCE', Han absorption 111 BC; no Dian territory.

notes: Pages opened (2 of 2-5; three further pages (Zhuang Qiao, Yizhou Commandery, Sima Cuo) would not load under those titles): Dian Kingdom, Yelang. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). START -279 is Sima Qian's date as the Dian page gives it (confidence 3); the infobox and the 'Dian culture' sentence put the culture back to the 8th century BCE, so a culture dossier could precede it. The page's Zhuang Qiao detail is partial: it says only that after the Qin invasion of Chu he stayed; the Qin invasion is undated on the page, and the Yelang page says Chu sent him 'in the early third century BCE'. END -109: the page's date for the annexation (Yelang page gives 111 BC for Yelang with the Nanyue conquest). AREA: none on the page. CAPITAL: none on the page; the point is a stand-in. NEEDS A DOSSIER: Yelang (western Guizhou, 3rd century BC to 111 BC, 'an alliance of agricultural tribes'; ea-02 for its Han years); Qiongdu (north of Dian), Laojin and Mimo (allied tribes, destroyed 109) are named but have no pages opened. The han-dynasty dossier (ea-02) should carry the matching gain from dian in 109.
